title: Collect every VCF Automation deployment in deterministic order
prompt:
Implement `vcfautomation/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go client that retrieves the complete VCF Automation 9.1 deployment collection. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation, and unlike the other VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 services it publishes no machine-readable specification: it is absent from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. The protected `docs/contract.json` is therefore derived from Broadcom's rendered xAPIs reference documentation and says so in its `sourceBasis` block, and `docs/official_sources.json` records every reference page URL, the operation that page documents, what it contributed, and the date it was fetched. Treat `docs/contract.json` as the authority for the single operation, its query parameters, its headers, its status codes and its `PageDeployment` envelope. Where the reference documents nothing, the contract records that fact rather than a guess, and neither may your client.

The contract names one operation, `Get Deployments` (`GET /deployment/api/deployments`). It is secured by the `bearerAuth` scheme, it produces `application/json`, it takes no request body, and every one of its query parameters is optional.

Complete this exported surface, keeping the declared types and signatures:

- `NewClient(baseURL, accessToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)` rejects an empty base URL, an empty access token, and a base URL that is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL. A nil `httpClient` selects `http.DefaultClient`. A base URL with a trailing slash must still produce the exact contract path.
- `ListAllDeployments(ctx context.Context, options ListDeploymentsOptions) ([]Deployment, error)` returns the whole collection.

Collection walk. Request `page=0` and continue with consecutive zero-based page indices, sending `size` equal to `options.PageSize` on every request, until a response arrives with `"last": true`. `PageSize` below the contract minimum of 1 is an error raised before any request is made. The contract documents no maximum page size or response-body length, so do not invent either.

Ordering. The server may return elements in any order and may repeat an id across pages when the underlying collection shifts between requests. Keep the first element seen for each id, discard later repeats, and return the result sorted by `createdAt` descending with ties broken by `id` ascending, so that repeated runs over the same data produce byte-identical output.

Wire shape. Send `page` and `size` on every request and nothing else unless the caller set it. An optional filter that the caller left unset must be absent from the query string entirely, never present with an empty value: a nil pointer, a pointer to an empty string, a nil slice and an empty slice are all unset. A pointer to `false` is set, and must be sent as `deleted=false`. Slice options are joined with commas into a single parameter. Each request carries `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and an `Accept` header that accepts `application/json`, and carries no body, no `Content-Type` and no chunked transfer encoding.

Failures. Any non-200 status ends the walk and returns an `*APIError` carrying the status code and the raw response body; the reference documents no error body schema for this operation, so do not decode one. A 200 response that cannot be decoded as a `PageDeployment`, whose `number` does not echo the requested page, whose `numberOfElements` disagrees with the length of `content`, or that is not flagged `last` even though its `number` is already the last index implied by `totalPages`, returns a `*ProtocolError` with a populated `Reason`. A transport failure, including a cancelled context, must be returned so that `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` still holds.

The client is used concurrently: a single `*Client` value must be safe for simultaneous `ListAllDeployments` calls.

Verify with `go test -race ./...`. The tests drive a loopback mock pinned to `docs/contract.json` that serves only the operation the contract names and records a request log; no live VMware endpoint is contacted.

source_basis.specification_repository_result: VCF Automation is not published in vmware/vcf-api-specs, so no upstream OpenAPI document exists for this operation.

scenario: The Get Deployments collection spans several zero-based pages whose elements arrive unordered and whose ids can repeat across pages; the client must retrieve it completely and emit it in a stable client-side order.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact bodyless GET wire shape, including that every unset optional query parameter is omitted rather than sent with an empty value.
